exercises.title: Thermostat command log
exercises.prompt:
A cheap thermostat controller used one shared variable and separate free functions for every action, something like a global `temp` changed by `up()`, `down()`, and `set(n)`. That style gets messy once more devices are added, so model the temperature as an object that owns its own state instead.

Write `Solution.run(String commands)`. `commands` holds one instruction per line: `SET n` sets the temperature to `n`, `UP` raises it by one degree, and `DOWN` lowers it by one degree. Every resulting temperature is clamped to the range 60 to 85 inclusive (a `SET` target is clamped too). After each instruction, record the temperature that results. Return every recorded value joined by newlines, in the order the instructions were given, with no leading or trailing blank line.

Example: commands `SET 70`, `UP`, `UP`, `DOWN` return `70`, `71`, `72`, `71` (one value per line).

exercises.title: Drone fleet fuel readout
exercises.prompt:
A small delivery-drone simulator models each drone as an object with its own fuel tank, while a separate shared counter tracks how many flights the whole fleet has completed.

Read the program in the editor and determine exactly what it prints to standard output. Give one value per line, in the same order the program prints them, with no extra spaces and no blank lines.

Every flight burns whole liters of fuel per ten kilometers traveled (integer division truncates any remainder), and every completed flight adds one to the shared fleet counter, no matter which drone object performed it.

exercises.title: Weekly reading goal tracker
exercises.prompt:
A small class tracks how many pages a reader finished on each day of the week and is supposed to report how many days met or beat a daily goal.

One line in the program below does not match that description, so the day count comes out wrong even though the code compiles and runs without crashing.

Read the class carefully and identify the single line responsible. Answer with that line's number, counting the very first line of the file as line 1.

exercises.title: Car rental total cost
exercises.prompt:
A car rental counter needs to price a single booking.

Design a `Vehicle` class that stores a `plate` (String) and a `dailyRate` (double), and a `Rental` class that associates a `Vehicle` with a `renter` (String) and a number of `days` (int); `Rental` computes the total price as `dailyRate * days`.

Write `Solution.rentalCost(String plate, double dailyRate, String renter, int days)` that builds the `Vehicle` and the `Rental` that references it, then returns the total price formatted to exactly 2 decimal places (no currency symbol). Assume `days` is never negative; zero days returns `"0.00"`.

Example: `rentalCost("ABC-123", 25.0, "Amina", 3)` returns `"75.00"`.

exercises.title: Playlist total time
exercises.prompt:
A music app stores a playlist of songs, each with a title and a length in seconds.

Design a `Song` class that stores a title and its length, and a `Playlist` class that is composed of a list of `Song` objects and can add up their lengths.

Write `Solution.totalTime(String[] titles, int[] seconds)` that builds a playlist from the two arrays (matching index belongs to the same song) and returns the total playing time as `"M:SS"` — minutes with no leading zero, then a colon, then seconds padded to two digits. An empty playlist returns `"0:00"`.

Example: `totalTime(["Intro", "Drive"], [50, 130])` returns `"3:00"` (50 + 130 = 180 seconds).

exercises.title: Payroll bonus total
exercises.prompt:
A small company pays a year-end bonus that depends on each employee's role.

Design an abstract `Employee` class holding a name and a base salary, with an abstract bonus calculation that each role overrides: a `Manager` bonus is 20% of base salary plus a flat 500; a `Developer` bonus is 10% of base salary plus 50 per completed project; an `Intern` bonus is always a flat 100, no matter the salary. Any other role earns no bonus.

Write `Solution.totalBonus(String[] roles, String[] names, double[] baseSalaries, int[] extra)` where `roles[i]` is `"manager"`, `"developer"` or `"intern"` (lowercase) and `extra[i]` is the completed-project count, meaningful only for developers. Build the matching employee for each row, read its bonus back through the base type, and return the sum of all bonuses formatted to 2 decimal places.

Example: `totalBonus(["manager"], ["Fahd"], [1000.0], [0])` returns `"700.00"` (1000 * 0.20 + 500).

exercises.title: Coffee order pricing
exercises.prompt:
A coffee stand prices an order using these steps, applied in exactly this order:

1. Start from the drink's base price and add $0.75 for every extra shot.
2. If the customer has a loyalty membership, take 10% off the running total.
3. If the running total is still more than $6.00 after that, add a flat $0.30 large-order fee.
4. Round to 2 decimal places and show it with a leading `$`.

Write `Solution.finalPrice(double basePrice, boolean memberDiscount, int extraShots)` that follows these steps in the given order and returns the price as a string.

Example: `finalPrice(6.00, false, 1)` returns `"$7.05"` (6.00 + 0.75 = 6.75, no membership, 6.75 is over $6.00 so add 0.30 = 7.05).

exercises.title: Battle Power Calculator
exercises.prompt:
A fantasy game computes battle power for each fighter before a match begins.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String battlePower(String type, int level)` that builds the matching fighter and returns its report.

Create an abstract class `Combatant` with an abstract method `int power()` and a concrete method `String report(String name)` that returns `name + ":" + power()`. Two subclasses extend `Combatant`: `Warrior`, whose `power()` is `level * 5`, and `Mage`, whose `power()` is `level * 3 + 20`. Each subclass stores the level passed into its constructor. If `type` is neither `"warrior"` nor `"mage"`, return `unknown`.

Example: `battlePower("warrior", 4)` returns `warrior:20`. `battlePower("mage", 4)` returns `mage:32`.

exercises.title: Checkout Fee Calculator
exercises.prompt:
An online store charges a different processing fee per payment method before totaling an order.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String checkoutTotal(String[] methods, double[] amounts)`. Each index pairs a payment method name with an amount charged through it. Define an interface `PaymentMethod` with a method `double fee(double amount)`, and three implementations: `CreditCard` charges `amount * 0.029 + 0.30`, `Wallet` charges `amount * 0.015`, and `Cash` charges nothing. Any other method name also charges nothing. For each pair, add `amount` plus its fee to a running total, then return the total formatted to exactly two decimal places.

Constraints: `methods.length == amounts.length`; the arrays may be empty, in which case the total is `0.00`.

Example: `checkoutTotal(new String[]{"creditcard", "cash"}, new double[]{100.0, 50.0})` returns `153.20`.

exercises.title: Library Checkout Rules
exercises.prompt:
A library checkout counter decides whether a member may borrow a book.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String checkout(boolean membershipActive, int copiesAvailable, int booksAlreadyOut)`.

Define three checked exceptions extending `Exception`: `InactiveMembershipException`, `OutOfStockException`, and `LimitReachedException`. Write a private helper method that throws, checking in this exact order: `InactiveMembershipException` when `membershipActive` is false, then `OutOfStockException` when `copiesAvailable` is 0 or less, then `LimitReachedException` when `booksAlreadyOut` is 3 or more (the borrowing limit). `checkout` must call the helper inside a `try` block and catch each exception type, returning its message; when nothing is thrown, return `approved`.

Exception messages, exactly: `inactive membership`, `no copies available`, `limit reached`.

Example: `checkout(true, 2, 1)` returns `approved`. `checkout(false, 2, 1)` returns `inactive membership`.

exercises.title: Average Temperature Log
exercises.prompt:
A weather station logs temperature readings throughout the day.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String averageTemperature(List<Double> readings)` that returns the average of all readings rounded to one decimal place, formatted as a plain number string. An empty list has no readings recorded, so return `0.0`.

Example: `averageTemperature(List.of(20.0, 22.0, 23.0))` returns `21.7`.

exercises.title: Recipe Quantity Scaler
exercises.prompt:
A home cook wants to scale a recipe up or down before shopping for ingredients.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String scaleRecipe(List<Double> quantities, double factor)`. Multiply every quantity by `factor`, round each result to two decimal places, and join them with commas and no spaces. An empty ingredient list returns an empty string.

Constraints: quantities are given in the same unit throughout; `factor` can be zero or greater.

Example: `scaleRecipe(List.of(1.0, 2.5), 2.0)` returns `2.00,5.00`.

exercises.title: Music Player State Tracker
exercises.prompt:
A music player starts stopped and reacts to a sequence of button presses.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String finalState(String[] commands)` that starts in state `STOPPED` and applies each command in order, then returns the state reached after the last one.

Transition rules:
- In `STOPPED`, only `"play"` has an effect, moving to `PLAYING`.
- In `PLAYING`, `"pause"` moves to `PAUSED` and `"stop"` moves to `STOPPED`; `"play"` has no effect.
- In `PAUSED`, `"play"` moves to `PLAYING` and `"stop"` moves to `STOPPED`; `"pause"` has no effect.

Any command not valid for the current state is ignored and the state does not change. `commands` may be empty, in which case the answer is `STOPPED`.

Example: `finalState(new String[]{"play", "pause", "play"})` returns `PLAYING`.

exercises.title: Delivery fee calculator
exercises.prompt:
A parcel courier app quotes a delivery fee depending on which vehicle carries the package.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String quote(String mode, double distanceKm)`. Each vehicle has its own base fee and per-kilometre rate: `bike` costs 2.00 plus 0.50 per km, `van` costs 5.00 plus 1.20 per km, `drone` costs 8.00 plus 0.30 per km. Return `<mode>:<fee>` with the fee rounded to 2 decimal places. For any other mode, return `invalid`. Support each vehicle through its own class behind one shared contract, so a new vehicle can be added later without touching the pricing logic of the others.

Example: `quote("bike", 5)` returns `bike:4.50`. `quote("car", 3)` returns `invalid`.

exercises.title: Coffee order pricing
exercises.prompt:
A cafe's till adds each extra to a drink one at a time, and the receipt must list them in the order they were rung up.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String order(String base, String[] addons)`. `base` is one of `espresso` (1.80), `latte` (3.20) or `tea` (2.00); each entry in `addons` is one of `milk` (+0.40), `syrup` (+0.60) or `shot` (+0.90), and the same extra can repeat. Apply the extras in the given order and return `<label>:<total>`, where `<label>` chains the names with a `+` in that order and `<total>` is the price rounded to 2 decimal places. Return `invalid` when the base or any extra is not recognised.

Example: a `latte` with `milk` then `syrup` returns `latte+milk+syrup:4.20`. A `tea` with no extras returns `tea:2.00`.

exercises.title: Shared ticket counter
exercises.prompt:
A help desk hands out ticket numbers to whichever staff member asks next, and every number must be used exactly once no matter which department is asking.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String process(String[] commands)`. Each entry in `commands` is either `NEW <department>`, which hands out the next ticket number (starting at 1, shared by every department) and reports `<department>:<number>`, or `COUNT`, which reports how many tickets have been handed out so far as `count:<n>` without using one up. Return one result per command, joined with commas, in the order the commands arrived. The same running total must be visible no matter which line of code asks for it.

Example: commands `NEW support`, `NEW sales`, `NEW support` produce `support:1,sales:2,support:3`.

exercises.title: Enemy wave spawner
exercises.prompt:
A game wave spawner reads a list of enemy codes and must create the right enemy for each one, letting every enemy type decide its own strength.

Write a class `Solution` with a static method `String spawnWave(String[] codes, int level)`. Each code is `goblin` (base power 5) or `dragon` (base power 40); an enemy's power is its base power times `level`. For each code, in order, produce `<code>:<power>`, or `unknown` for any other code, then join the results with commas. An empty `codes` array returns an empty string. Structure the enemy types and how each is built as separate classes, so adding a new enemy later needs no changes to the existing ones.

Example: codes `goblin`, `dragon` at level 1 produce `goblin:5,dragon:40`. A `dragon` at level 0 produces `dragon:0`.

exercises.title: Photo booth session pricing
exercises.prompt:
A mall photo booth prices a single session using these steps, applied in exactly this order:

1. Start from the session's base price and add $0.75 for every extra photo shot taken.
2. If the customer has a booth membership, take 10% off the running total.
3. If the running total is still more than $6.00 after that, add a flat $0.30 printing fee.
4. Round to 2 decimal places and show it with a leading `$`.

Write `Solution.finalPrice(double basePrice, boolean memberDiscount, int extraShots)` that follows these steps in the given order and returns the price as a string.

Example: `finalPrice(6.00, false, 1)` returns `"$7.05"` (6.00 + 0.75 = 6.75, no membership, 6.75 is over $6.00 so add 0.30 = 7.05).
